newsitem.title: USA: NYS court says NYC needs council okay on hospitals.
newsitem.headline: NYS court says NYC needs council okay on hospitals.

text.p: A New York State Supreme Court judge ruled Wednesday that New York City Mayor Rudolph Giuliani must get approval from the City Council to privatize three city hospitals.
Council leaders have steadily opposed the mayor's plan and went to court to assert their right to review.

State Supreme Court Justice Herbert Posner said in the ruling that the City Health and Hospitals Corp (HHC) "was born out of the city's need to salvage a hospital system that was floundering. If HHC, likewise, is confronted with a system nearly drowing in red ink, defendants' response cannot be simply to jump ship."

The decision means that the Council would get to pass judgment on a proposed 99-year lease of Coney Island Hospital in Brooklyn to PHS NEW YORK, a for-profit company tied to Primary Health Systems Inc of Wayne, PA.

The deal, which was reached late last year and which the city said would save it up to $100 million immediately, has been waiting for approval from state regulators, a process that can take 18 months or longer.

The Giuliani Administration also was seeking bidders for the Elmhurst and Queens Hospital Centers in Queens, and a press spokeswoman for the mayor was not immediately available to comment on whether it would appeal the ruling.
The state supreme court is the lowest level of the state's three courts.

In its lawsuit, the Council claimed that it had the right to review the lease for the Coney Island Hospital. Until 1989, that right rested with the now defunct Board of Estimate, whose powers were divided between the mayor and the Council under a revised charter, as required by a court decision.
The judge ruled that the Council, as the successor to the Board of Estimate, has the right to review the hospital deal.
